title: Story
description: A single interactive storybook set in a world. Holds the narrative spine, the page-by-page spreads (full-page image + embedded text), the interactive elements, and the reading-level targets used to age-adapt the language.

age_band.description: READER ability band: who will read (or be read) the words. Drives reading_level defaults — sentence length, words per page, word choice. Distinct from target_year (what the story is about). 'grown-up' means the story is written for an adult reader (rich vocabulary, full prose, no word caps).

target_year.description: CONTENT age: the single age (in years) the story itself is pitched at — interest level, humor, stakes, themes. One number, not a range. A book can have target_year 7 (a seven-year-old's jokes and jeopardy) at age_band 5-7 reading ability.

reading_level.description: Targets that drive language adaptation and are verified by the validator.

target_fk_grade.description: Target Flesch-Kincaid grade level for the whole book.

decoding_focus.description: Phonics/sight-word focus, e.g. 'CVC words, short a; sight words: the,is,a'.

decodable.description: If true, restrict text to taught phonics patterns + listed sight words.

themes.description: Optional. Recurring ideas/flavours the book plays with (e.g. adventure, mischief, friendship) — NOT lessons to teach.

moral.description: Optional and usually unnecessary. At most a quiet feeling the book leaves behind — NEVER a lesson spelled out on the page. Most fun books should leave this empty (see methodology/fun-first.md).

affirms_rules.description: Ids of the world `rules` this book deliberately engages (see world.rules). Makes the world's laws traceable/reviewable per book; the validator checks each id resolves.

characters.description: Characters appearing in this story and the evolution stage each is at HERE (locks both personality and appearance for this book).

stage.description: evolution.stage id from the character; defaults to the character's base appearance.

spine.description: The story spine (Pixar/Kenn Adams). Drives structure before any page is written.

interactions_summary.description: Quick list of the interactive beats so the editor can balance pacing.

tags.description: Browse/filter tags (the 'tags' level of world -> story -> tags).

text.description: The words ON the page (embedded into the full-page image).

prompt.description: Scene description ONLY (no style/character tokens — the generator injects world art_style + character appearance_tokens automatically).

characters_present.description: slugs of characters in frame; their appearance_tokens get injected.

file.description: Relative path to the generated image.

text_zone.description: Where to keep the composition clear for embedded text (overrides world default).

vocabulary.description: Target/new words introduced on this page (for the glossary & pedagogy checks).

reading_notes.description: Tips for the adult co-reader (question to ask, sound to emphasise).

interaction.description: A short, playable game embedded in the page — a fun break that's part of the romp, about what just happened on this page. Not a hidden drill.

type.description: Interaction type — a short, playable, FUN break that belongs to this page. NEW BOOKS USE REAL GAMES: the arcade-* family — real-time games on an embedded game engine (fullscreen over the page art, physics, a game loop; every noun is skinned from the story — see $defs/arcadeSpec): arcade-catch (steer & catch what falls), arcade-flap (tap to fly through gaps), arcade-run (auto-run & jump, reach the finish), arcade-pop (pop the right drifting things), arcade-toss (slingshot into the target), arcade-steer (drag to steer, collect & dodge), arcade-snake (classic snake — slither, gobble, grow), arcade-shoot (gentle space shooter — steer & zap), arcade-maze (real-time maze — swipe to scoot through, assist reveals the trail), arcade-build (stack the swinging pieces into a tower), arcade-whack (whack-a-mole — bop them before they duck), arcade-bounce (breakout — bounce the ball, smash the wall). The branching 'choice' (a narrative fork) is also allowed, sparingly. ALL OTHER TYPES ARE LEGACY — kept so previously published books keep playing; do NOT use them in new books (no drag-and-drop, no find-in-picture, no tap boards, no quizzes). When no arcade mechanic fits, pick a different beat or skin a mechanic differently — don't fall back to a legacy type.

prompt.description: The instruction shown to the reader.

skill.description: Optional INTERNAL label only — never shown to the child. Default 'engagement'. If a game happens to exercise a reading skill (phonemic-awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) you may tag it, but fun is the point, not skill coverage.

data.description: Type-specific payload. Shape depends on 'type' — see methodology/interactivity.md for every shape. On-art types use normalized coords {at:{x,y}} with x,y in 0..1. For type 'custom', data MUST match $defs/customGameSpec.

steps.description: Optional multi-beat chain: each entry is a mini-interaction played in turn; the whole game is solved only after the last beat. Steps may NOT nest their own steps.

difficulty.description: Optional hint to the renderer to scale the challenge (e.g. sliding-puzzle 2x2 vs 4x4).

reward.description: Optional theming for the collectible the child earns by solving this game. Without it the reader awards a default sticker automatically.

label.description: Name of the sticker, e.g. 'Dragon Scale'.

id.description: Stable id so the same collectible can recur across a series.

arcadeSkin.description: A thing in an arcade game, skinned from the story: an emoji string, or {emoji, label} (label doubles as the accessible name).

arcadeSpec.description: Payload for the arcade-* games (real-time engine games, fullscreen over the page art). Every noun is an arcadeSkin straight from the story — the mechanic is the engine, the story is the skin. Required keys per type (enforced by scripts/lib/checks/interactivity.py): arcade-catch needs `catch`; arcade-pop needs `pop`; arcade-toss needs `projectile`+`target`; arcade-flap needs `player`; arcade-run needs `player`+`collect`; arcade-steer needs `player`+`collect`; arcade-snake needs `player`+`food`; arcade-shoot needs `player`+`targets`; arcade-maze needs `player`; arcade-build needs `blocks`; arcade-whack needs `whack`; arcade-bounce needs `ball`+`bricks`. All games are always winnable: no fail states, and the runtime adds a rubber-band assist ladder.

player.description: The thing the child controls (usually this page's hero). In arcade-bounce it's the paddle.

avoid.description: Things to dodge — touching one is a funny bonk, never a penalty.

obstacle.description: (arcade-flap) what the gap columns are made of (clouds, trees…).

collect.description: (arcade-run / arcade-steer) the thing to gather; (arcade-maze) optional treats sprinkled deep in the maze.

food.description: (arcade-snake) what the snake gobbles to grow.

body.description: (arcade-snake) optional skin for the growing tail segments (default: friendly beads).

shot.description: (arcade-shoot) what the player fires (default ✨) — a splash, a snowball, a beam of light…

exit.description: (arcade-maze) the exit marker the player scoots toward (default 🏁).

size.description: (arcade-maze) maze size — cozy 7×5, normal 9×6, big 11×7. interaction.difficulty maps onto this too.

blocks.description: (arcade-build) the pieces that swing overhead and get stacked into the tower.

whack.description: (arcade-whack) the things that pop up from the burrows to bop.

bricks.description: (arcade-bounce) what the smashable wall is made of.

rows.description: (arcade-bounce) rows of wall (1–3; 6 pieces per row).

goal.description: How many to catch/pop/collect/land/gobble/zap/stack/bop to win. Keep it small (4–12): a game is a fun BREAK.

gates.description: (arcade-flap) gaps to fly through to win.

speed.description: Pace. Use 'gentle' for under-7s. interaction.difficulty maps onto this too.

how.description: Optional one-line how-to shown on the intro card, in the story's voice.

avoid_line.description: Optional funny line shown when the child touches an avoid-thing.

customGameSpec.description: A declarative game an author (or LLM) invents from primitives — no code. Elements (draggables / dropzones / hotspots / targets / toggles) plus a win condition. There is NO fail state in the model, so a custom game is winnable by construction; the reader adds a hint ladder + auto-solve as the final backstop.

stage.description: 'scene' plays on the page art; 'board' plays in a plain card. Auto-detected from element coords if omitted.

elements.description: Every interactive thing in the game; each needs a unique id.

group.description: (draggable) bucket key a dropzone may accept.

win.description: How the game is won. Combine with all/any/not for composite wins.

coord.description: A point on the page art, normalized 0..1 (origin top-left). Legacy percent (0..100) is auto-detected.
